statement: Under C81's actual transitive boundary-fixed source hypothesis for a closed discrete free proper interior disk operator group, the actual quotient has a locally finite triangulation whose lifted closed vertex stars form a null family in the original closed disk. The pointwise stabilizer of its full lifted one-skeleton in the original relative centralizer is topologically isomorphic, by restriction and labelled equivariant pasting, to the product of the chosen triangle homeomorphism groups relative to their boundaries. Coordinatewise Alexander deformation contracts that entire actual subgroup while fixing the identity.
depends_on: C81 exact invariant metric covering and compact-core translate control; C64 compact-covering lemma for actual open evaluation; verified Rado Section 3 Hilfssatz 2 and Haver Lemma 1 with k=0; explicit nullity, labelled pasting, inverse, product-topology and Alexander proofs
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), exact null lifted triangulation and contractible skeleton stabilizer in the remaining discrete-operator level-zero question.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The actual transitive relative subgroup is retained as a hypothesis. The covering, its original deck labels, the chosen lifted triangles and every restriction/pasting inverse are displayed. Original-boundary control follows from the proved null family, without extending an arbitrary operator or an interior conjugacy to the circle.
computational_checks: This qualitative theorem has explicit constructions and uniform estimates and makes no finite classification or numerical claim. The new primary sources were opened and read at the exact stated lemmas. Mechanical checks cover JSON validity, unique display tags, balanced displayed environments and absence of accidental escape characters.
notes: The actual infinite product is justified by the finite-large-triangle property, which controls both maps and inverses in the original disk topology. No deformation of every original sphere family to the skeleton stabilizer is claimed, and no inverse-limit conclusion is drawn from the finite-label homotopy isomorphisms of C81. The remaining controlled vertex/edge deformation keeps C12 open in the general scope. Previously accepted fragments are unchanged.
